source.title_on_document: Human–GenAI collaboration across creative phases: Cognitive mechanisms shaping novelty and usefulness

supplement.where: No online supplement is mentioned. Appendices A to I are inside the PDF (pp. 11-14): interviewee profiles, interview questions, coding framework, task texts, manipulation materials, scale items.
supplement.holds: Nothing outside this PDF. The appendices hold task wording and manipulation instructions only; no extra statistics.

paper_design_summary: Study 1 interviews 20 creative professionals. Studies 2a (N = 42) and 2b (N = 44) are within-subject lab experiments with university students: each person wrote two product-innovation proposals, one with the SparkDesk chatbot during one phase (idea generation in 2a, idea elaboration in 2b) and one alone, with task and condition order randomized. Study 3 (N = 198 employees, online, preregistered) randomly assigned people in a 2 x 2 design to use ChatGPT in the idea generation phase or in the idea elaboration phase of an advertising-proposal task, crossed with a high or low perceived-GenAI-intelligence manipulation; three marketing experts rated novelty and usefulness of the proposals.

assignment.what_was_assigned: Nothing; semistructured interviews about how professionals use GenAI in creative work
assignment.quote: We collected data for this study through semistructured interviews.

participants.exclusions: None reported; recruitment stopped at data saturation.
participants.who: Professionals in creative roles with substantial experience integrating GenAI into their work; mean age 27.8
participants.country: not stated (authors in China; paid in CNY)
participants.quote: A total of 20 interviews were conducted, meeting common qualitative sampling thresholds

ai_tool.name_model: Various GenAI tools used by interviewees in their own work
ai_tool.how_used: Self-reported use in ordinary work; no tool provided by the study

task.description: Semistructured interviews of about 50 minutes, coded in NVivo with grounded-theory coding

studies.label: Study 2a (lab, within-subject, GenAI in idea generation phase vs working alone)

assignment.what_was_assigned: Order of the two conditions (GenAI collaboration during the idea generation phase vs working independently) and order of the two tasks
assignment.quote: Both the task order and the human–GenAI collaboration order were randomized to control for order effects.

arms.name: GenAI condition (idea generation phase)
arms.description: Used SparkDesk during the 10-min idea generation phase; then elaborated the ideas for 10 min without search engines or GenAI (Appendix E)

arms.name: H condition (independent)
arms.description: Both 10-min phases without search engines or GenAI

participants.exclusions: 45 university students recruited; 3 failed an attention check; final sample 42. The paper does not say whether the 3 were dropped before or after assignment.
participants.who: University students (59.5 percent bachelor's, 33.3 percent master's, 7.1 percent doctoral), mean age 21.17, recruited from online and offline campus groups, paid 40 CNY
participants.country: not stated (paid in CNY; Chinese LLM SparkDesk; authors in China)
participants.quote: Three participants failed the check, resulting in a final sample of 42.

ai_tool.how_used: Participants were allowed to collaborate with the GenAI tool during the 10-min idea generation phase only; the elaboration phase was done without GenAI.

task.description: Product-marketing creativity task adapted from Noy and Zhang (2023): as a product manager, write a creative proposal of at least 100 words to make a new mouse/milk/headphone/bicycle product more innovative. Two tasks of equal rated difficulty, one per condition.
task.duration: 20 min per task (10 min idea generation + 10 min idea elaboration); session about 20 min per the text

outcomes.name: Novelty of proposal (expert-rated)
outcomes.question: with_ai
outcomes.measure_detail: Consensual assessment technique: three marketing experts, blind to purpose, hypotheses, and conditions, rated novelty (degree of innovation and uniqueness of the proposal and advertising copy); mean of three experts per participant. ICC2 H = 0.82, GenAI = 0.85. Scale: the paper says measures are 7-point unless noted.

contrasts.reported: Novelty (H condition) M = 5.44, SD = 0.55; Novelty (GenAI condition) M = 6.05, SD = 0.59; N = 42. No test of the direct difference is reported. Indirect effect of collaboration on novelty through cognitive flexibility = 0.17, 95% CI = [0.033, 0.341] (5000 bootstrap replications).

outcomes.name: Usefulness of proposal (expert-rated)
outcomes.question: with_ai
outcomes.measure_detail: Same three marketing experts; usefulness = potential for practical implementation and ability to solve real problems and create maximum value. ICC2 H = 0.87, GenAI = 0.82.

contrasts.reported: USEN (H condition) M = 5.21, SD = 0.45; USEN (GenAI condition) M = 5.37, SD = 0.52; N = 42. No test of the difference is reported.

studies.label: Study 2b (lab, within-subject, GenAI in idea elaboration phase vs working alone)

assignment.what_was_assigned: Order of the two conditions (GenAI collaboration during the idea elaboration phase vs working independently) and order of the two tasks
assignment.quote: The randomization procedures in Study 2b were identical to those used in Study 2a.

arms.name: GenAI condition (idea elaboration phase)
arms.description: 10-min idea generation phase without GenAI; then 10-min idea elaboration phase with the GenAI tool allowed (Appendix F)

arms.name: H condition (independent)
arms.description: Both 10-min phases without search engines or GenAI

participants.exclusions: 45 university students enrolled; 1 failed the attention check; final sample 44. Recruited separately from Study 2a (no overlap).
participants.who: University students (63.6 percent bachelor's, 34.1 percent master's, 2.3 percent doctoral), mean age 21.16
participants.country: not stated (authors in China; same recruitment as Study 2a, paid in CNY)
participants.quote: One participant failed the attention check, resulting in a final sample of 44.

ai_tool.how_used: Participants were allowed to collaborate with the GenAI tool only during the 10-min idea elaboration phase, after generating preliminary ideas alone.

task.description: Same product-marketing creativity tasks as Study 2a (Appendix D): write a creative proposal of at least 100 words to make a new product more innovative.
task.duration: 20 min per task (10 min generation + 10 min elaboration)

outcomes.name: Usefulness of proposal (expert-rated)
outcomes.question: with_ai
outcomes.measure_detail: Same consensual assessment as Study 2a; usefulness ICC2 H = 0.91, GenAI = 0.93.

contrasts.reported: USEN (H condition) M = 5.49, SD = 0.39; USEN (GenAI condition) M = 5.89, SD = 0.39; N = 44. No test of the direct difference is reported. Indirect effect of collaboration on usefulness through cognitive overload = 0.14, 95% CI = [0.056, 0.222] (5000 bootstrap replications).

outcomes.name: Novelty of proposal (expert-rated)
outcomes.question: with_ai
outcomes.measure_detail: Same three experts; novelty ICC2 H = 0.79, GenAI = 0.74.

contrasts.reported: Novelty (H condition) M = 5.31, SD = 0.47; Novelty (GenAI condition) M = 5.43, SD = 0.49; N = 44. No test of the difference is reported.

studies.label: Study 3 (online 2 x 2: GenAI in generation vs elaboration phase, x perceived GenAI intelligence)

assignment.what_was_assigned: Creative phase in which participants collaborated with ChatGPT (idea generation vs idea elaboration), crossed with a perceived-GenAI-intelligence manipulation (high vs low, via a news-report text and a recall task)
assignment.quote: A randomized 2 × 2 between-subjects design assigned participants to one of four experimental conditions.

arms.name: Idea generation phase x high perceived GenAI intelligence
arms.description: ChatGPT collaboration during the idea generation phase; read a news text describing GenAI as highly intelligent and recalled such experiences

arms.name: Idea generation phase x low perceived GenAI intelligence
arms.description: ChatGPT collaboration during the idea generation phase; read a news text describing GenAI intelligence as rudimentary

arms.name: Idea elaboration phase x high perceived GenAI intelligence
arms.description: ChatGPT collaboration during the idea elaboration phase; high-intelligence news text

arms.name: Idea elaboration phase x low perceived GenAI intelligence
arms.description: ChatGPT collaboration during the idea elaboration phase; low-intelligence news text

participants.exclusions: 205 full-time employees recruited by purposive and snowball sampling; 7 failed attention checks and were excluded; 198 analyzed. The paper does not say whether exclusion came before or after assignment, and gives no per-cell counts.
participants.who: Full-time employees (59.1 percent male, mean age 27.60; 75.3 percent bachelor's, 19.7 percent master's; services 26.8 percent, IT 26.3 percent, manufacturing 18.7 percent); base pay 20 CNY plus rewards for exceptional solutions
participants.country: not stated (paid in CNY; limitations say most participants were based in East Asia, p. 10)
participants.quote: After seven participants who failed attention checks were excluded, 198 valid responses remained for analysis.

ai_tool.name_model: ChatGPT, accessed through a custom online system integrating a GenAI interface via API
ai_tool.how_used: Participants used ChatGPT within a custom system during only one phase of the task: the idea generation phase (first 10 min) or the idea elaboration phase (second 10 min), depending on arm. Manipulation materials adapted from Study 2.

task.description: As a product manager for Apple's iPhone division, write advertising copy / an advertising plan (200+ words) for a leather flip phone case, prioritizing novelty and practicality (Appendix G).
task.duration: 20 min (10 min idea generation + 10 min idea elaboration)

outcomes.name: Novelty of proposal (expert-rated)
outcomes.question: with_ai
outcomes.measure_detail: Same measurement approach as Study 2 (three marketing experts, consensual assessment); novelty ICC2 = 0.82.

contrasts.reported: Table 3: correlation of collaboration phase (1 = idea elaboration, 0 = idea generation) with novelty r = -0.30** (N = 198); pooled novelty M = 4.60, SD = 0.89. Arm means not reported. Indirect effect of phase (1 = idea generation, 0 = idea elaboration) on novelty through cognitive flexibility = 0.16, SE = 0.06, 95% CI = [0.065, 0.283] (PROCESS Model 4, 5000 bootstraps). No direct or total effect reported.

outcomes.name: Usefulness of proposal (expert-rated)
outcomes.question: with_ai
outcomes.measure_detail: Same measurement approach as Study 2; usefulness ICC2 = 0.84. Moderated mediation by perceived GenAI intelligence also reported (INDEX = 0.26, SE = 0.13, 95% CI [0.019, 0.516]).

contrasts.reported: Table 3: correlation of collaboration phase (1 = idea elaboration, 0 = idea generation) with usefulness r = 0.42** (N = 198); pooled usefulness M = 4.52, SD = 0.90. Arm means not reported. Indirect effect of phase (1 = idea elaboration) on usefulness through cognitive overload = 0.35, SE = 0.08, 95% CI = [0.205, 0.518]. No direct or total effect reported.

eligibility.reason: Study 3 randomly assigned 198 analyzed employees (205 recruited) to use ChatGPT in the idea generation vs idea elaboration phase, a different AI configuration (codebook ai_design example: ideas versus refinement), with expert-rated novelty and usefulness of the proposals (p. 7). Studies 2a (42) and 2b (44) randomize the order of AI vs no AI within person but fall below 50 people. Study 3 has no no-AI arm, so it supplies only an ai_design contrast.

one_line_finding: In Study 3 (N = 198), using ChatGPT in the elaboration rather than the generation phase correlated with lower expert-rated novelty (r = -0.30) and higher usefulness (r = 0.42) (p. 8, Table 3), with indirect effects via cognitive flexibility (0.16, CI [0.065, 0.283]) and overload (0.35, CI [0.205, 0.518]).
open_questions: Which output the experts rated (preliminary ideas after phase 1 or final ideas after phase 2) is not stated; ai_available_when_produced is coded 'mixed' because AI was available in only one of the two phases. If only final ideas were rated, Study 2a's GenAI arm and Study 3's generation-phase arm produced the scored text after AI was removed, which may argue for after_ai.

Study 3 reports no arm-level means or direct/total effect of phase on novelty or usefulness; only point-biserial correlations (Table 3) and bootstrapped indirect effects. Per-arm counts are not given (Table 3 mean of the phase dummy is 0.49).
Studies 2a and 2b report condition means and SDs but no test of the AI vs no-AI difference on novelty or usefulness, only indirect effects through self-reported mediators.

Treatment/control labels for the Study 3 ai_design contrast are a coding choice: the elaboration-phase arm is called treatment here because Table 3 codes it 1; the paper codes generation = 1 in the novelty mediation.
notes: Cognitive flexibility and cognitive overload are self-reported mediators (7-point scales) and are not listed as outcomes. The perceived-GenAI-intelligence manipulation in Study 3 changes beliefs about the same tool, not the AI configuration; no direct effect of it on novelty or usefulness is reported, only moderated mediation (H6a INDEX = 0.14, SE = 0.08, CI [-0.018, 0.313]; H7a INDEX = 0.26, SE = 0.13, CI [0.019, 0.516]; p. 8-9) and an interaction on cognitive overload (F(1, 194) = 5.06, p < 0.05; Fig. 2, p. 9). A G*Power analysis called for 146 participants (p. 7). The markdown conversion scrambles Tables 1-3; all numbers were checked against PDF pages 6-8.
